extracted.intended_audience: aspiring writers, periodical authors, reviewers, and the literate public interested in producing or judging essays, newsletters, and short topical pieces
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and selecting material for short periodical essays and news-letters (allegory, topical reflection, gossip/‘whispers’, character sketches, and critical reviews). Emphasises observational stance, sustained allegory, selection of newsworthy items, and modes of moral/character portrayal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained allegory
rubrics_metrics.description: An Allegory so well carry'd on, that it cannot but be very pleasing to those who have a Taste of good Writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a consistent, extended comparison (e.g., the garden as education) that maps leaves/flowers/fruit to stages of mental development and qualities of mind. Vary the components (types of leaves/flowers/fruits) to illustrate differences of talent and culture; avoid breaking the comparison mid-course. Examples in the text: mapping Italian/French/German 'leaves' and 'flowers' to national intellectual traits; note risks such as over-fondness of particular flowers (over-attention to ornament at the expense of fruit).

rubrics_metrics.name: News article 'whispers' — core ingredients
rubrics_metrics.description: The two chief Qualifications in an Article of News ... first, as they are private History, and, in the next place, as they have always in them a Dash of Scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a successful short news item or whisper include (a) intimacy/secretiveness that makes the reader feel 'let into' something private, and (b) a titillating scandalous element. Suitable materials: sickness of persons in high posts, twilight visits by ministers, clandestine courtships and marriages, secret amours, losses at play, applications for places and their outcomes. These kinds of particulars make a news-item more than ordinary gossip and attract readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make readers feel 'in the secret' (reader positioning)
rubrics_metrics.description: The great Incentive to Whispering is the Ambition which every one has of being thought in the Secret, and being look'd upon as a Man who has Access to greater People than one would imagine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style and presentation should cultivate the sensation that the reader is privileged — use low-voiced tells, suggestive hints rather than full revelations, and present details as conveyed under a veil of secrecy. Distribution timing and repeated early publication at popular venues (analogy: coffee-houses; morning/evening timings) increase spread and make readers repeat and claim the rumor as their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity for critical reviews — 'Works of the Unlearned'
rubrics_metrics.description: A Review that treats ‘An Account of the Works of the Unlearned’ — i.e., take as subjects those productions and authors who make an eminent figure in the Illiterate World.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing critical or satirical reviews, prioritize publications and authors whose pretensions or party-agendas make them notable despite lack of genuine learning: party-authors, puffed editors, commentators of little knowledge. Use these targets to produce instructive or amusing criticism; you may also review foreign accounts that unworthily noticed trivial or ignorant works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational stance: curiosity, detachment, and speculative delight
rubrics_metrics.description: To be ever unconcerned, and ever looking on new Objects with an endless Curiosity, is a Delight known only to those who are turned for Speculation ... value Things only as they are the Objects of Speculation, without drawing any worldly Advantage to themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a lightly detached, curious narrator stance: observe broadly and record minutiae for their interest rather than practical consequence. This stance turns everyday scenes into material for amusement or the improvement of the mind and makes every face/object yield expressive material. The essay demonstrates this by roaming markets, coaches, coffee-houses, and the Exchange, noting social types and small actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid social types and small, specific details to enliven scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: It was very easie to observe by their Sailing, and the Countenances of the ruddy Virgins, who were Super-Cargoes, the Parts of the Town to which they were bound ... The Silk-worms ... are indulged by the Tradesmen; for tho' they never buy, they are ever talking of new Silks, Laces and Ribbands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate scenes with recognizable social archetypes (gardener fleets, fruit-wenches, silk-worms, hackney-coach customs) and concrete gestures/cant (coachmen signs, canto/phrases like 'Silk-worm') to signal character and class quickly. Small material details (laced shoe, coach-window, a bed among 'lumber') provide strong sensory anchors and convey social life efficiently. Avoid abstract generalities when a single striking detail will do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depicting misery and tragedy by concrete indignities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bitterness of being the Scorn and Laughter of base Minds, the Anguish of being insulted by Men hardened beyond the Sense of Shame or Pity, and the Injury of a Man's Fortune being wasted, under Pretence of Justice, are excellently aggravated in the following Speech ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To render bankruptcy or ruin affecting, enumerate tangible humiliations and losses (seizure and sale of plate, destruction or sale of domestic ornaments, the very bed of conjugal memory thrown into common lumber) and include the voices/jests of those who profit. Show how social contempt compounds material loss. Use vivid dramatic speech (as Otway's Pierre does) to amplify the emotional weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of modesty — distinguish true modesty from false modesty
rubrics_metrics.description: True Modesty is ashamed to do any thing that is repugnant to the Rules of right Reason: False Modesty is ashamed to do any thing that is opposite to the Humour of the Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When characterising modesty, make explicit whether a character's restraint arises from principle (true modesty: guided by prudence, religion, reason) or from mere fashion and fear of singularity (false modesty: leads to imprudent or even criminal compliance). Demonstrate consequences: false modesty pushes individuals to lend beyond means, recommend unsuitable people, or comply with vice to avoid standing out; true modesty restrains wrongdoing. Use behavior (what the character refuses or accepts) to show which kind of modesty they possess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and moral depiction: prefer sincere virtue but recognise social prudence
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypocrisie cannot indeed be too much detested, but at the same time is to be preferred to open Impiety. The due Mean to be observed is to be sincerely Virtuous, and at the same time to let the World see we are so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In moral or religious portrayals, aim for sincerity as the ideal, but acknowledge social realities that sometimes make appearance preferable to blatant impiety. Avoid glorifying hypocrisy, but in narrative choices recognise that public demonstration of virtue (within reason) can be socially useful. This is both ethical advice and a guideline for how characters’ religious/moral comportment should be presented: honest piety is best, ostentation or blatant impiety are censured, and hypocritical performance is undesirable though less harmful than open irreligion.
